policy: merge overlapping incident windows; ignore merged blips <60s; exclude maintenance ONLY when announced >=24h before start
bug_report: A tenant is disputing their monthly SLA report: our report says 99.7% uptime for the period, but their ops team swears the service met 99.9% and their own monitoring agrees. downtime_minutes is producing a bigger number than the outage time the tenant actually experienced. A failing repro is at tests/test_regression.py. Fix downtime_minutes so the report matches real downtime, without breaking existing behaviour.
non_guessable: decision lives in git history (a documented commit), broken by a misleading 'perf' regression commit; git log/blame is the shortcut
decision_subject: fix: align downtime_minutes with the SLA credit accounting addendum
decision_rationale: Tenants were disputing uptime reports because downtime_minutes summed raw alert windows. Per the SLA credit addendum: overlapping or touching incident windows merge before summing so concurrent alerts never double-count; a merged outage under 60 seconds is a monitoring blip and counts for nothing (the threshold applies to the merged window, not per raw incident); and maintenance reduces downtime only when announced at least 24 hours before its start (announced_at) - short-notice maintenance still counts as downtime, customers do not eat credits for surprise maintenance.
